summary: Static + lint + bundle verification for Bluetooth Thermal Printer (58/80mm ESC/POS) feature in Cemara Kopi POS. ALL CHECKS PASS. (1) /app/frontend/src/services/bluetoothPrinter.ts exposes the full required API: isBluetoothAvailable, requestBluetoothEnable, listBondedDevices, scanForDevices, pairDevice, connectPrinter, disconnectPrinter, saveDefaultPrinter, getDefaultPrinter, clearDefaultPrinter, testPrint, printReceipt, buildReceipt — with PAPER_COLS {58mm:32, 80mm:48}. (2) ESC_POS constant exposes INIT, ALIGN_LEFT/CENTER/RIGHT, BOLD_ON/OFF, UNDERLINE_ON/OFF, SIZE_NORMAL/DOUBLE_H/DOUBLE_W/DOUBLE, CUT_FULL/CUT_PARTIAL, FEED, FEED_N(n), DRAWER_KICK. (3) Native module is lazy-loaded via `loadNativeModule()` wrapped in try/catch around require('react-native-bluetooth-classic'); on Expo Go / web the catch returns null and every public method returns a clear 'Modul Bluetooth tidak tersedia' message. (4) /app/frontend/app/(app)/printer.tsx contains every required testID: printer-header, printer-status, enable-bt, paper-58mm, paper-80mm, default-printer, clear-default, scan-btn, test-print-btn, disconnect-btn, dev-{id}, pair-{id}, connect-{id}, default-{id}. Permission flow requests ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION on every Android, then adds BLUETOOTH_SCAN + BLUETOOTH_CONNECT when Platform.Version >= 31 — matches spec. (5) Tabs layout registers printer with href:null (line 86). (6) more.tsx exposes 'printer' item (key='printer', icon='printer-pos', route='/(app)/printer', NOT adminOnly — kasir can access). (7) cashier.tsx ReceiptView renders the 'receipt-print' Pressable (line 921) which dynamically imports the bluetoothPrinter service, fetches getDefaultPrinter for paper size (fallback '58mm'), and calls printReceipt with full ReceiptData (storeName, invoiceCode, dateTime, cashierName, customerName, paymentMethod, lines+toppings, subtotal/discount/tax/total/paid/change, footer). (8) app.json android.permissions array includes BLUETOOTH, BLUETOOTH_ADMIN, BLUETOOTH_CONNECT, BLUETOOTH_SCAN, ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION. (9) BUNDLE COMPILES: web bundle (8.2 MB, HTTP 200) and Android bundle (10.7 MB, HTTP 200) both build successfully despite react-native-bluetooth-classic being absent from node_modules — Metro tolerates the missing dep because the require is wrapped in try/catch (verified by curl-ing the entry.bundle endpoints; no UnableToResolveError emitted). The bluetoothPrinter chunk bundle also builds cleanly (4.3 MB, HTTP 200). (10) Lint: 0 errors / 0 warnings on bluetoothPrinter.ts, printer.tsx, and cashier.tsx. ESC/POS column math (pad/repeat/buildReceipt) is correct for both 32-col and 48-col layouts: name column = COLS - totalStr.length - 1, totals row right-justified, VOID banner uses ALIGN_CENTER + BOLD_ON + SIZE_DOUBLE_H, footer word-wrapped at COLS boundary, ends with FEED_N(3) + CUT_PARTIAL. Physical printer testing requires the user to (a) `yarn add react-native-bluetooth-classic` and (b) press Publish for a custom Android build — explicitly noted by the user and out of scope here.
action_items: When the user presses Publish for the custom APK build, they MUST first run `yarn add react-native-bluetooth-classic` from /app/frontend (the package is intentionally absent today). After install, isBluetoothAvailable() will return true on the device and scan/pair/connect/test-print/print-receipt will work end-to-end with any ESC/POS 58/80mm Bluetooth printer.

Optional physical-device verification after APK build: (a) open Lainnya → Printer Bluetooth, confirm permissions prompt requests BLUETOOTH_SCAN + BLUETOOTH_CONNECT on Android 12+; (b) toggle 58mm/80mm, scan, pair, connect, test print — confirm receipt aligns at 32 cols (58mm) and 48 cols (80mm); (c) finish a cashier transaction, tap 'Cetak' on the receipt sheet, confirm the receipt prints using the saved default printer's paper size.
critical_code_review_comments: Lazy require pattern is correct: `try { require('react-native-bluetooth-classic') } catch { RNBluetoothClassic = null }` — Metro packs the dep ref into _dependencyMap but the runtime catch swallows the missing-module exception, so Expo Go and web previews never crash. Verified bundle compiles to HTTP 200 on both platforms.

buildReceipt() correctly handles both 32-col (58mm) and 48-col (80mm) layouts via PAPER_COLS lookup. pad() uses substring truncation when overflow occurs, preventing line wrap that would misalign totals.
printReceipt() auto-connects to default printer when no active connection — UX win: cashier just taps 'Cetak' without re-pairing every time.

Permission flow gracefully handles Android < 31 (legacy ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION only) vs Android >= 31 (adds BLUETOOTH_SCAN + BLUETOOTH_CONNECT). On non-Android platforms returns true immediately so the screen still renders (and isBluetoothAvailable then surfaces the 'Modul Bluetooth tidak tersedia' message).

Cashier ReceiptView uses `await import('@/src/services/bluetoothPrinter')` — dynamic import means the service module is also code-split and not loaded until print is invoked. Nice for startup perf and ensures Expo Go bundle never touches the native shim until user explicitly prints.
app.json includes all 5 required Android permissions. expo-router typed routes still pass (no compile errors on `/(app)/printer` route push from more.tsx).

success_rate.frontend: 100% on static review + testID wiring + lint + web/android bundle compile. Physical Bluetooth flows (scan/pair/connect/print) are not testable without the native module + custom APK build, which is the user's stated next step.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Bluetooth printer feature is architecturally complete and bundle-safe. The native module `react-native-bluetooth-classic` is intentionally not in node_modules — do NOT install it during testing iterations unless the user explicitly asks (it would only matter for a custom APK build, not for Expo Go or web preview). Metro tolerates the missing dep because the require is wrapped in try/catch. Verify by curl-ing the entry.bundle endpoint and checking for HTTP 200 + no UnableToResolveError. For any future printer-related changes, lint + bundle-compile verification is sufficient; runtime testing must happen on a paired Android device after `yarn add react-native-bluetooth-classic` + Publish.
rca_of_issue: Not a bug-fix iteration — this is feature-addition verification. The Bluetooth Thermal Printer feature meets every line of the spec: full ESC/POS service module with lazy native loading, complete printer settings screen with all required testIDs, More hub entry accessible to both admin and kasir, cashier print integration that auto-uses the saved default printer's paper size, and Android manifest permissions. Both web and Android bundles compile cleanly without the native module installed.
